edges.source: Proteasome Subunit and Assembly-Factor Loss of Function

edges.description: Recurrent fever driven by the sustained interferon response rather than by an inflammasome cycle — which is what distinguishes this from the classic periodic fever syndromes.
Acral violaceous lesions, the characteristic cutaneous sign of a type I interferonopathy.
Progressive loss of subcutaneous fat, which in this disease follows the panniculitis rather than occurring independently — the sequence is inflammation first, then loss.
Progressive muscle wasting, part of the same progressive-loss phenotype.
Contractures developing as the inflammatory and atrophic process crosses joints.
Anaemia of chronic inflammation, microcytic here.

nodes.description: Pernio-like acral inflammatory lesions are a characteristic skin finding in the PRAAS/Nakajo-Nishimura end of the spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Nakajo-Nishimura syndrome and related proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Phenotypes of NNS patients are periodic fever, pernio-like rash, nodular erythema-like eruptions, and lipomuscular dystrophy, especially in the upper body, leading to the characteristic long, clubbed fingers.

nodes.description: PRAAS variants disrupt proteasome subunit expression, assembly, and mature proteasome function, reducing proteolytic capacity.

evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: Function evaluation revealed that these mutations variably affect transcription, protein expression, protein folding, proteasome assembly, and, ultimately, proteasome activity.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of eight novel proteasome variants in five unrelated cases of proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: All newly identified mutations substantially impact the steady-state expression of the affected proteasome subunits and/or their incorporation into mature 26S proteasomes.

nodes.description: Progressive fixed joint limitation is a recurrent disabling musculoskeletal manifestation across the PRAAS spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: PSMB8 encoding the β5i proteasome subunit is mutated in joint contractures, muscle atrophy, microcytic anemia, and panniculitis-induced lipodystrophy syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We performed homozygosity mapping in two recently reported pedigrees from Portugal and Mexico with an autosomal-recessive autoinflammatory syndrome characterized by joint contractures, muscle atrophy, microcytic anemia, and panniculitis-induced lipodystrophy (JMP).

nodes.description: Progressive lipodystrophy is one of the most distinctive shared features across CANDLE, NNS, and JMP presentations.

evidence.reference_title: Disease course and treatment effects of a JAK inhibitor in a patient with CANDLE syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Clinical manifestations include presentation in the first year of life, episodes of fever accompanied by erythematous skin lesions, progressive lipodystrophy, violaceous periorbital swelling and failure to thrive.

nodes.description: Protein kinase R senses proteotoxic stress in PRAAS and amplifies type I interferon and inflammatory signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Protein kinase R is an innate immune sensor of proteotoxic stress via accumulation of cytoplasmic IL-24.
evidence.snippet: Here, we identified protein kinase R (PKR) as an innate immune sensor for proteotoxic stress.

evidence.reference_title: Protein kinase R is an innate immune sensor of proteotoxic stress via accumulation of cytoplasmic IL-24.
evidence.snippet: under conditions of proteasome dysfunction, PKR sensed the cytoplasmic accumulation of a known interactor, interleukin-24 (IL-24).

nodes.description: Lobular panniculitis is part of the inflammatory skin and adipose-tissue phenotype in PRAAS, especially in JMP/CANDLE presentations.

nodes.description: Recurrent febrile inflammatory episodes are a core systemic manifestation across the PRAAS spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Nakajo-Nishimura syndrome and related proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Phenotypes of NNS patients are periodic fever, pernio-like rash, nodular erythema-like eruptions, and lipomuscular dystrophy, especially in the upper body, leading to the characteristic long, clubbed fingers.

nodes.description: Patient immune and stromal cells show a sustained interferon-response program that remains a central molecular hallmark across PRAAS genotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production.
evidence.snippet: Patient-isolated hematopoietic and nonhematopoietic cells exhibited a strong IFN gene-expression signature, irrespective of genotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in proteasome subunit β type 8 cause chronic atypical neutrophilic dermatosis with lipodystrophy and elevated temperature with evidence of genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: Microarray profiles and monocyte STAT-1 activation suggested a unique IFN signaling signature, unlike in other autoinflammatory disorders.

nodes.description: Inherited or de novo loss-of-function defects in proteasome catalytic subunits or assembly factors initiate the PRAAS disease cascade.

evidence.reference_title: Contribution of the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) to the Pathogenesis of Proteasome-Associated Autoinflammatory Syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: By definition, PRAAS are caused by inherited and/or de novo loss-of-function mutations in genes encoding proteasome subunits such as PSMB8, PSMB9, PSMB7, PSMA3, or proteasome assembly factors including POMP and PSMG2, respectively.

nodes.description: Impaired proteasome function causes accumulation of ubiquitinated or misfolded proteins, engaging stress pathways including the unfolded protein response.

evidence.reference_title: Contribution of the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) to the Pathogenesis of Proteasome-Associated Autoinflammatory Syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: Disruption of any of these subunits results in perturbed intracellular protein homeostasis including accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins which is accompanied by a type I interferon (IFN) signature.

evidence.reference_title: Contribution of the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) to the Pathogenesis of Proteasome-Associated Autoinflammatory Syndromes (PRAAS).
evidence.snippet: One promising candidate for triggering type I IFN under sterile conditions is the unfolded protein response (UPR) which is typically initiated in response to an accumulation of unfolded and/or misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (also referred to as ER stress).
